measuredOn: Windows (Vitest 4 projects consolidation in app/vitest.config.ts; freshly measured with verify-coverage-baseline.ps1 per-package runs; every package above prior baseline — net optimization, not a relaxation)
ciPlatform: ubuntu-latest (v8 coverage is execution-path based; numbers are cross-platform deterministic)
policy: Coverage baseline gate — numbers must not regress. If a metric drops below the value recorded here (minus the v8 run-to-run tolerance), the gate fails (exit 1). A second assertion requires skipped tests == 0 so .skip / .todo cannot silently mask a regression. To raise the bar, update this file with freshly measured numbers + a new measuredAt/masterSha; never lower a number without an explicit baseline re-baseline decision.
toleranceNote: v8 coverage is execution-path based and mostly cross-platform deterministic, but a few async setup/teardown paths execute non-deterministically between runs. On @agenthub/shared two stable states were observed locally (lines 71.57 vs 71.59, a 2-statement / 1-function delta); web and desktop were bit-identical across runs. The 0.08pp tolerance absorbs this run-to-run variance with margin while still catching any deleted test that covers more than a handful of unique statements (a real cheat), which moves coverage by well over 0.08pp. If CI shows larger drift, raise this field — do not lower baseline numbers.
